data.name: Mughith
data.gender_notes: Mughith is used as a male name in Islamic naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: In Arabic, Mughith means 'rescuer' or 'savior'. It is a name with deep spiritual meaning in Islam, signifying deliverance from adversity and guidance towards the right path. The name Mughith carries the meaning “Rescuer, Savior” and is chosen by families in Islamic traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Arabic tradition and is also used in Arabic, Urdu, Persian. Parents who choose Mughith usually hope their child will grow to embody rescuer, savior and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: A symbol of hope and deliverance.
data.etymology: Mughith belongs to the Arabic linguistic tradition and is used in Islamic naming. Its recorded meaning is “Rescuer, Savior.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Mughith total 5, giving a life-path number of 5. Number 5 is linked with Mercury and with the qualities of freedom, adaptability and curiosity.

in_english.name: Mughith
in_english.meaning: blessed with abundant life, preventer of evil, giver of prosperity, bringer of good fortune, successful in good deeds
in_english.long_meaning: The name Mughith is derived from the Arabic root 'M-G-Th', which means to bless with abundant life, to prevent evil, to give prosperity, to bring good fortune, and to be successful in good deeds. It is mentioned in the Quran as a name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful. In Islamic tradition, Mughith is considered a name that conveys blessings, prosperity, and good fortune.

This name was commonly given to children born during hardships or times of crisis, as a reminder of God's protection and provision. It also carries the message of hope and optimism, reminding individuals that even in the face of adversity, God is with them and will bring them through to the other side.

historical_references.reference: Mughith ad-Din Muhammad ibn Bahadur was a Sultan of the Deccan Sultanate of the Bahmani dynasty. He ruled from 1422 to 1435 CE and is best known for his military conquests and patronage of architecture and learning. He expanded the Bahmani sultanate's territories, defeating Rashtrakutas and Vijayanagara forces.
historical_references.context: Sultan of the Deccan Sultanate of the Bahmani dynasty

historical_references.reference: Mughith Shah, also known as Mughith Al-Din Muhammad, was a Sultan of the Ghaznavid Empire from 1131 to 1148 CE. He was the eldest son of Bhaktiyar Khawar, and succeeded his father upon his death. Mughith Shah is remembered for his military victories against the Seljuks, Khurramites, and Khwarazmian Shia rebels.
